To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

human activities have greatly increased the rate of nitrogen inputs to terrestrial ecosystems, and that these increased inputs are causing serious environmental problems, including losses of soil fertility, losses of biological diversity (especially of nitrogen-efficient plants and animals), and long-term losses of coastal marine fisheries.

human alterations of nitrogen inputs to terrestrial ecosystems have increased the rate of nitrogen transfer through terrestrial food webs, and have caused losses of biological diversity and changes in the composition, dynamics, and function of terrestrial ecosystems.
human alteration of the nitrogen cycle has caused serious environmental consequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
human alterations of the global nitrogen cycle and their environmental and societal consequences.
the environmental consequences of human alterations of the global nitrogen cycle.

the effects of human activities on the nitrogen cycle and the effects of these changes in nitrogen availability on the functioning and dynamics of terrestrial, freshwater, estuarine, and nearshore marine ecosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the human alteration of the global nitrogen cycle has had a major and largely negative effect on terrestrial, freshwater, estuarine, and marine ecosystems, and has had a major positive effect on agricultural production.

the human alteration of the global nitrogen cycle has been substantial and is still increasing; that it has had serious environmental consequences, and that it will continue to do so unless the rate of N inputs into ecosystems is substantially reduced.

the human alterations of the global nitrogen cycle have had and will continue to have major and long lasting effects on the environment, and that the magnitude of these effects is comparable to those of the human alteration of the global carbon cycle.

human alteration of the global nitrogen cycle is a major environmental problem that has serious consequences for both the natural environment and human welfare.
human activities have increased the availability of nitrogen in many terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecosystems, and this has caused major environmental problems.

the environmental consequences of the human alteration of the nitrogen cycle are substantial, long term, and global in scope.
